narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job. In practical terms, among employees with a similar profile, about 85 out of 100 are predicted to leave, so the organization treated your retention risk as high and denied the promotion on that basis. Your gender, age, and health issues were not used in this prediction.

The strongest reason was your total work experience of 6–10 years. Compared with employees predicted to stay, this range was less common than 1–5 years, and it was the single largest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. The second strongest was that you reported having other job opportunities; most employees predicted to stay did not report such opportunities, so this added strongly to the leave signal. The third was your 1–5 years of experience in your current organization, which also contributed to the leave prediction in your overall profile.

These factors do not prove you will leave, but they made the model’s warning strong enough to affect the promotion decision. The organization should discuss your career path, retention, recognition, workload, and development needs before using this prediction as a final judgment. You should clarify your intentions, ask what would make you stay, and request a concrete promotion and development plan so the decision is based on a fuller conversation rather than the prediction alone.
